newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's largest Plock refinery mulls debt issue.
newsitem.headline: Poland's largest Plock refinery mulls debt issue.

text.p: Poland's largest refinery Petrochemia Plocka SA is mulling a debt issue on Polish and international markets to finance a part of its $800 million, two-year investment programme, its president said.

"We are thinking about issuing, on the Polish and later on international markets, debt instruments that would serve as additional financing for Petrochemia's investments," Konrad Jaskola told a news conference on Monday. Jaskola told Reuters the issue would account for about one-third of $350-400 million worth of investment due to be financed through different types of borrowing.

"Investment paid for through debt financing will amount to $350-400 million over the next two years, with one third financed through debt issues and the rest with a syndicated loan and funds from the National Environmental Protection Fund," Jaskola said.
Jaskola declined to give any specifics about the issue's type or timing saying only that it could take place at the end of this year or early in 1998.
He added the refinery wanted to carry out the debt issue without mandating a lead manager.
Jaskola also said that the refinery would need to look at its profit margins following the February 14 removal of government controls on fuel prices before deciding when to set the borrowing.
He said Plock was in talks with several Polish banks on the syndicated loan including the Pekao SA group, Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy SA (WBK) and Bank Handlowy SA.

Plock, with its present crude processing capacity of more than 10 million tonnes a year, processes 75-percent of imported crude oil, has a 66-percent share in the domestic production of petrol and diesel and a 57-percent share of Poland's liquid fuels market.
